question: In which year was the Bahmani Empire established?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1347 AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bahmani Empire was established in **1347 AD** by **Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah**.
 
• This empire was located in the **Deccan region** of South India, with its initial capital at Gulbarga and later at Bidar.
 
• The foundation of the Bahmani Empire marked the beginning of a long period of Muslim rule in the Deccan.
 
• The Bahmani rulers were known for their significant contributions to the **art, architecture, and culture** of the Deccan region.
 
• The kingdom was one of the major Muslim states in India and played a crucial role in the political and cultural history of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deccan Sultanates**

 
 
• The Bahmani Empire eventually fragmented into five Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Golkonda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, and Berar.
 
• These sultanates were prominent in the 16th and 17th centuries and were known for their contributions to Indo-Islamic culture and architecture.
 
• They played a significant role in the resistance against the Mughal expansion in the Deccan.
 
 
 
• **Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah**
 
 
• The founder of the Bahmani Empire, originally known as Zafar Khan, was a former governor under the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• He declared independence from the Delhi Sultanate and established the Bahmani kingdom.
 
• His reign marked the beginning of the Bahmani dynasty, which ruled the Deccan for nearly two centuries.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Contributions**
 
 
• The Bahmani rulers were great patrons of architecture, contributing to the development of Indo-Islamic architecture in the Deccan.
 
• Notable structures include the Jama Masjid in Gulbarga, the Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur, and the Bidar Fort.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Cultural Developments**
 
 
• The Bahmani Empire facilitated trade and cultural exchanges between the Deccan and other parts of the world, including Persia, Arabia, and Africa.
 
• The Bahmani court was known for its cosmopolitan culture, which included scholars, poets, and artists from different regions.
